subject: HW onramp: ETA variance, cloud backfill & vendor handoff
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alice Cheng <alice@stratusai.com>, sales@cloudscale.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HW onramp: ETA variance, cloud backfill & vendor handoff

Hi Alice / CloudScale team —

Quick note as we finalize the DL-8721 onboarding runway: your OEM (Dell) signaled a +/- 6 week variance on the GPU shipment window this morning. Given StratusAI’s committed launch date and the reserved capacity assumptions in the SOW, I want to align on two things:

1) Confirmation of the most conservative ETA you have from Dell (PO/line item level).
2) Whether CloudScale can commit to a temporary burst/backfill contract (region: us-west-2) to cover the earliest 6-8 week stretch if hardware slips.

We should avoid a hard start-date dependency on chassis-level delivery if we can bridge with cloud capacity and then perform a targeted carve-in once hardware arrives. Please see the attached ETA_matrix_q2-v2.xlsx for the scenario table I put together (best / nominal / conservative).

Action items I’m proposing by EOD Friday:
- Alice: confirm Dell quote line and whether they can provide a firm build week (not just ship window).
- CloudScale: give a high-level pricing sketch for a 6-8 week on-demand backfill (estimated vCPU/GPU hours + ingress costs).
- Marissa/Karthik: prepare a go/no-go checklist for customer comms & onboarding sequence if the conservative ETA triggers fallback.

Thanks — I want to ensure StratusAI has a smooth customer experience without surprise delays.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: ETA_matrix_q2-v2.xlsx
From: Alice Cheng <alice@stratusai.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, John Dell <john.dell@dellequipment.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HW onramp: ETA variance, cloud backfill & vendor handoff

Jonas —

Thanks for flagging. We just heard from Dell this morning: their current build window is mid-June through early July, but they explicitly warned of potential shifts if subcomponent supplies re-route. I’ve asked John to push for a firm production week; he replied that they can provide a production commitment by next Wednesday but cannot firm the shipment booking until that confirmation.

Meanwhile, StratusAI is open to a short-term cloud backfill for the launch milestone; the customer has a hard marketing commit we can’t miss. If CloudScale puts a pragmatic price on a 6-week burst, we’ll take it.

I’ve attached the OEM_quote_summary.pdf John sent — it’s high level but includes the P/Ns and expected queues.

—Alice
Alice Cheng
Head of Cloud Ops, StratusAI
alice@stratusai.com

From: sales@cloudscale.com <sales@cloudscale.com>

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HW onramp: ETA variance, cloud backfill & vendor handoff

Hi Alice, Jonas, Marissa —

Appreciate the context. We can offer a short-term dedicated backfill in us-west-2 with guaranteed instance availability for GPUs (A100 equivalent) for a 6-week window. High-level pricing (ballpark):
- Reserved-style 6-week commitment (guaranteed instances): $4,800 / GPU-week
- Data egress and storage: separately metered; estimate $2,200 total for anticipated transfer from Redwood staging
- Rapid provisioning lead-time: 48–72 hours once agreement signed

We’ll need a brief SLA addendum to guarantee capacity during the window. If you want, we can draft a one-page bridge contract and an invoice schedule — we can also support a staged handoff where Redwood migrates workloads back on-prem once Dell hardware is live.

Let me know if you want a written quote and I’ll push it to legal today.

—Chris Nguyen
CloudScale Account Exec
sales@cloudscale.com

Jonas / team —

Short update from Dell supply: we’ve escalated DL-8721 line to our build desk. We can commit to a tentative build week of 2027-06-18, but that becomes firm only when component receipts clear (expected windows next Tue/Wed). If you need a firm shipment week now, we can issue a formal hold-and-commit with a non-refundable deposit to prioritize your line (tradeoff: cost + lead-time certainty).

If you prefer CloudScale bridging, we can coordinate a partial ship-to staging address to speed acceptance testing and reduce the carve-over work once the fleet arrives. I’ll send the hold-and-commit paperwork if you confirm.

Regards,

Team —

Thanks everyone — summary and recommended path forward below:

Summary:
- Dell tentative build week: 2027-06-18 (may firm next Wed).
- CloudScale can provide a 6-week guaranteed bridge with 48–72h provisioning. Ballpark cost: ~$4.8k / GPU-week.
- StratusAI needs covering for launch; they’re okay with a short-term backfill.

Recommended plan (approved by sales leadership):
1) Execute CloudScale bridge contract for a 6-week window starting 2027-06-15; include staged provisioning and a carve-in playbook. (Jonas to own counter-signature with CloudScale)
2) Ask Dell for a hold-and-commit quote for two chassis (DL-8721) and evaluate deposit option only if Dell cannot firm the build week by next Wednesday. (Alice to coordinate)
3) Ops runbook: Redwood & Stratus agree on test IP ranges, DNAT rules, and a one-day cutover checklist to migrate traffic from CloudScale to the on-prem fleet. (Karthik to author)

I’ll draft the bridge PO and the customer comms note for the launch. If no objections by EOD tomorrow, we’ll spin the CloudScale SOW and route for signatures.

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
